title: The Foolish Dominie

full_text:
In a crowded schoolroom in Cairo, twenty mischievous boys sat upon palm mats on a hot summer afternoon, weary of memorizing long lists of irregular verbs under the watchful eye of their strict dominie.

The cleverest boy in the class whispered a daring plot to his companions: 'Our master is a hypochondriac who fears illness above all things. If we all play our parts with solemn faces, we shall have a holiday before the hour of noon!'

As the master sat upon his chair, the first boy stepped forward to recite his lesson, looked at the master’s face with theatrical horror, and gasped: 'O master! May heaven preserve you! Why are your cheeks so pale, and why do your eyes look so glassy?'

The dominie frowned: 'Silence, boy! I am perfectly well; recite your lesson!'

A few minutes later, the second boy approached with his slate, dropped it in alarm, and cried: 'Alas, master! You are shivering! Your lips are blue, and a dreadful fever has seized your countenance!'

The dominie began to feel a strange chill down his spine. He touched his forehead: was it truly hot?

One by one, all twenty boys approached, each wailing with louder lamentation, begging the master to lie down before he collapsed from the terrible contagion!

Overcome by the power of suggestion, the healthy schoolmaster’s knees began to shake; his head throbbed, his vision blurred, and he groaned in genuine agony!

'Help me home, my children!' moaned the dominie. 'A pestilence has struck down your poor master!'

The boys helped him to his house, tucked him beneath five heavy woollen blankets, closed the shutters, and ran shouting into the sunshine to enjoy three days of joyful holiday, while the poor dominie drank bitter herbal broths, completely cured of his health by twenty determined schoolboys.
moral: Power of suggestion and hypochondria can convince even a healthy man of imaginary illness.
